newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ivernia mine construction to start early '97.
newsitem.headline: Ivernia mine construction to start early '97.

text.p: Irish-based mining company Ivernia West Plc said on Tuesday it expected the construction phase of its Lisheen zinc-lead mine in the Irish midlands to start in early 1997.
The mine is a joint-venture with Minorco.

At the company's annual meeting, Chairman Clayton Love said planning permission for the mine had been granted in August but a number of objections had been lodged since then and were being considered by the authorities.
"The company is confident that all outstanding issues will be resolved speedily and that the construction phase of the mine can commence early in 1997," he said.
Love said negotiations to secure limited-recourse bank financing of $173 million to fund 70 percent of the total project development cost of $247 million were now at an advanced stage.

He said considerable progress had been made in negotiating sales contracts with European and North American zinc smelters, and there were clear indications of a strong demand for Lisheen's high-quality zinc concentrates.

"The joint venture partners are in the process of securing frame contracts for up to 80 percent of the output from the Lisheen mine for the first five years of production. These contracts should be in place by the end of the year," Love said.
